To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
xanthine dehyrogenase and xanthine oxidases are similar enzymes in terms of structure and mechanism, and that the dehydrogenase contains only a single iron-sulphhur centre.

the enzyme Veillonella xanthine deydrogenase is an oxidoreductase, that it is similar in its catalytic properties to the enzyme xanthin oxidase, that its catalytic mechanism is similar to the oxidase, that it has a molybdenoiron cofactor, that it contains flavin and that the enzyme contains iron-sulfur centres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action and the structure of xanthine oxidoreductase, a molybdenium-containing flavoprotein with a binuclear iron-sulphhur centre.
the elucidation of structure-function relationships of the xanthine oxidizing enzymes.
the study of molybdate and tungstate containing enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
xanthine dehyrogenase and milk xanthine-oxidase are similar in structure and in their reaction mechanisms.
, in the dehydrogenase, the molybdeno-flavin-iron-sulphur centre system is very similar to that in the oxidase but the iron-sulphide centre is different.
the xanthine dehydragenase from V. alcalescens has a structure similar to that of xanthine oxidoreductase from milk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dehydrogenase has the same molybdeno-enzyme centre as milk xanthine deoxyhydrogenase, but lacks the iron-sulphide centre of the latter.
the two enzymes are similar but not identical.

the dehydrogenase, like xanthine oxidases, contains a molybdenyl centre and two flavins, but differs from the oxidases in having only one iron-sulfur centre and lacking the ability to oxidize substrates directly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to xanthine oxidoreductases, Veillonella xanthine dehyrogenase is a flavoprotein.
the dehydrogenase, in contrast to the oxidase, has only a single iron-sulphide cluster.
we have shown for the first time that the molybdenums in these two enzymes have the same ligands in the same arrangement.
